title: Horreum · the model
headline: One relational model, drawn once
standfirst: The same model the article argues about, laid out as tables you can open. Every field carries the reason it exists, every table names who is allowed to write it, and the five invariants sit against the rows they actually hold. Nothing here is a screenshot of an admin panel: it is the shape of the data, which is the part that decides everything else.
description: An interactive schema for Horreum: products, size-level variants, the movement journal, imports and receipts, with the invariant and the writer named on every table.
alt: A schema of six tables. An import run holds import items, which target variants. A product holds its variants, a variant holds its movements, and a receipt item also points at a variant. The product total is drawn back from the variants as a derived edge, because it is recomputed from them rather than typed.
note: Column names follow the running system; types are given as they behave rather than as PostgreSQL spells them. Quantities and codes shown anywhere on this page are invented, as they are in the article.
legend: Written by a person or a document. The only numbers anybody actually observed.
Computed from rows that own the truth. Never typed, and rebuildable from scratch.
Used to attach an incoming row to a variant. Never generated by us.

entities.name: inventory_import_runs
entities.label: Import run
writers: The import, when a file is applied
The rollback, to mark a run reversed
entities.why: A file is evidence and the rows it produced are an interpretation of it, so the run is kept as its own record. Mode belongs here rather than on the file: whether a missing article means unchanged or means gone is a property of the supplier channel, decided once, never inferred per upload.
entities.reads: The rollback reads this table to find out what a run claimed to have done.

entities.name: inventory_import_items
entities.label: Import item
entities.sub: one row of the file, resolved
writers: The import, inside the transaction that applies the file
entities.why: Keeping the quantity before and after beside the identifier that matched is what makes an undo possible at all. matched_by is the rung of the identity ladder that hit, and it is stored because a match by the manufacturer's article and a match by a per-size code are not the same claim.
entities.reads: The rollback compares new_qty with what the variant holds now, and refuses if they differ.

entities.name: products
entities.label: Product
writers: A person, for the descriptive columns
The stock function, for the two derived ones, and nothing else
entities.why: Two identifiers sit here because they answer different questions. article is ours and is printed on the tag a customer reads back over the phone; factory_article belongs to the manufacturer and is what a supplier price list is matched on. Collapsing them into one tidy SKU is the obvious move and the wrong one.
entities.reads: A listing page filters on is_in_stock so that sixty cards do not run sixty subqueries.

entities.name: product_variants
entities.label: Variant
entities.sub: the cell: one product, one size
writers: One stock function, called by the sale, the import and the hand correction
Nothing else may write a quantity
entities.why: This row is the only quantity in the system anybody actually counted, and everything upward of it is arithmetic. active keeps a size that is not stocked apart from a size stocked and currently at zero, which a single stock column on the product cannot express. The barcode is empty across all ≈7,100 variants and its index is partial, so today it indexes nothing and costs nothing.
entities.reads: Availability is a cell above zero. Search covers every code here, including the one that is computed rather than stored.

entities.name: stock_movements
entities.label: Movement
fields: import | receipt | sale | return | adjust | writeoff
writers: The same single stock function, in the same transaction as the quantity it describes
entities.why: delta is the change that was asked for and qty_after is what actually resulted. Both are kept because both paths clamp at zero: two units sold against one in stock and one sold against one leave the same row behind, and the disagreement between these two columns is the only evidence that a clamp happened.
entities.reads: Turnover and dead stock are read from this journal rather than kept as counters of their own, so there is no second number to fall out of step.

entities.name: goods_receipt_items
entities.label: Receipt item
entities.why: Not one of the five supplier file shapes contains a purchase price: they send what they would like you to sell at. Cost is therefore resolved in a fixed order, and a weighted average over posted receipts is the first and best step of it.
entities.reads: Every valuation the system reports carries the step that produced it, because a receipt-based cost and a rule-derived one must not be confused downstream.

edges.label: sum of active variants, recomputed in the same transaction

invariants: The product total equals the sum of its active variants after every committed movement.
Recomputation inside the same transaction as the movement.
Every change of a quantity leaves exactly one journal row, carrying its cause.
A single write path: sale, import and hand correction call one function.
No value used for matching is ever generated by us.
Omission: the barcode generator is never run, and the size code is computed on read.
Every reported valuation carries the step that produced it.
The resolver returns provenance with the number.
An ambiguous row is held. It is never completed with a default.
The absence of a fallback in the parser.
